title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 429
paragraphs: About her death, as about the death of Smerdis, two different stories are told. The Greeks say that Cambyses had pitted a lion cub against a puppy, and this wife of his was also watching. When the puppy was being overpowered, another whelp, its brother, broke its chain and came to its aid; and having become two instead of one, the whelps then got the better of the cub. Cambyses was pleased at the sight, but she, sitting beside him, began to weep. Cambyses noticed and asked her why she wept, and she said she had wept when she saw that the whelp had come to help its brother, because she remembered Smerdis and perceived that no one would come to his aid. The Greeks say it was for this saying that she was killed by Cambyses. The Egyptians, however, say that as they were sitting at table, the wife took a lettuce and pulled off the leaves all round, then asked her husband whether the lettuce was more beautiful stripped like this or with leaves on, and he said “with leaves on.” She then spoke thus: “Yet you once produced the likeness of this lettuce, when you stripped bare the house of Cyrus.” Moved to anger, he leapt upon her, and she, being pregnant, miscarried and died.
